problems.title: Spot interval DP

options: Minimum cost to merge adjacent stones

hints: Merging or splitting contiguous pieces with neighbour-dependent costs.

parts.prompt: Which balloon is burst last in the optimal order?

problems.title: First or last?
problems.statement: Why condition on the LAST balloon in Burst Balloons?

options: Until it bursts, it separates the two sides, and when it does its neighbours are the interval ends

problems.solution: Conditioning on the first burst makes the sides adjacent, so they interact.

problems.title: Cut a stick

parts.prompt: Cost of cutting in the given order 1, 3, 4, 5?

hints: The first cut costs the full length 7.
problems.solution: Given order: 7 + 6 + 4 + 3 = 20. Best: 16 (for example cut 3 first, then 5, then 1 and 4).

problems.title: Loop order
hints: dp[i][j] reads dp[i][k] and dp[k][j] for i < k < j.
problems.solution: i ascending would read dp[k][j] with k > i before it's computed.

problems.title: Complexity
problems.statement: Interval DP with n = 400 and O(n) transitions.
problems.solution: About 1.1 × 10⁷, fine in C++ and borderline in pure Python.

problems.title: Stone game
problems.statement: Two players alternately take a pile from either end of a row; dp[i][j] = the maximum score difference the player to move can secure on piles i..j.
hints: After your move, the opponent becomes the player to move.
problems.solution: The difference formulation (negamax) avoids tracking two scores, and is common in game DP.
